findings.title: V2 canManage() grants global group management for the VIEW scope
findings.body: `canManage()` falls back to `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so a view-only permission on the "all groups" resource is enough to pass it. This is the check behind `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (`auth.groups().requireManage()`). An admin who was granted only `view` on all groups can therefore create top-level groups. The per-group `canManage(GroupModel)` correctly uses only `MANAGE`, and the V1 equivalent requires the manage-users role, so this looks like a copy-paste from `canView()`. The Javadoc in `GroupPermissionEvaluator` repeats the same wrong contract. No test covers a VIEW-only admin attempting a manage operation. Change the call to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses resource IDs where group IDs (resource names) are needed
findings.body: In V2 the authorization resource for a group is named after the group ID (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`, and `hasPermission` looks it up with `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`). The callback here passes `groupResource.getId()`, which is the resource's own UUID, to `hasPermission`. That lookup by name never matches, so evaluation silently falls back to the generic "Groups" type resource and ignores the per-group permission. The method then adds `groupResource.getId()` to the result set, but callers (`UsersResource.searchForUser`, `getUsersCount`, `BruteForceUsersResource`) treat the values as group IDs for `UserModel.GROUPS` and `getUsersCount(..., groupIds)`. The result is wrong or empty sets and wrong user counts. For searches, the group restriction is not applied in the query, so the later per-user `canView` filter runs after `first`/`max` pagination and returns short or empty pages. The new test only checks the unpaginated search, where the post-filter hides the problem. Use `groupResource.getName()` for both the evaluation and the result, and skip the type-level resource whose name is "Groups".

findings.title: Possible NPE when the Groups type resource does not exist
findings.body: `getResourceTypeResource` returns null when the "Groups" resource has not been created. This happens for realms whose admin-permissions client was initialized before this change, because `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns early when the client already exists and never adds the group scopes or resource. It also returns null if the schema is not active. The code passes that null straight into `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`, which throws an NPE and turns every group permission check into a 500. Add a null check and return false.

findings.title: Incorrect Javadoc on requireManageMembers and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission
findings.body: The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers` says it throws when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false, but it actually delegates to `canManageMembers`. The Javadoc for `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` says it returns a "Stream of IDs" while the method returns `Set<String>`. The `canManage()` Javadoc documents VIEW as sufficient for manage, which is wrong behavior (see the canManage finding above). Fix these descriptions.

findings.title: Weak and missing assertions in group permission tests
findings.body: `testManageGroupMembership` only checks that `joinGroup` does not throw. It does not verify that bob became a member, and it has no negative case such as a different group without the permission. The test suite also has no case showing that a VIEW-only permission on all groups cannot create or modify groups, which would have caught the `canManage()` bug. No test covers the users count endpoint or paginated user search, which use `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` and would expose the resource-ID/group-ID mix-up.
